note: Each check's criterion as committed before its recorded run, with every amendment made before it. Where the source names a person, another project, a session or a local path, a role in square brackets stands in its place, and `replacements` lists each.

versions.text: | G2 | **Two annotations agree.** Ensembl (ENST00000359596.8) and RefSeq (NM_000540.3) give the same coding exon boundaries on GRCh38. MANE Select means they should | Any coding boundary differs. The difference is investigated before going on |

criteria.source: the M01 mission's criteria table (a working note, not public), at each commit

versions.text: | G3 | **The map is complete and exact.** Every coding base maps to exactly one position in one codon: 15,117 bases, 5,038 codons plus a stop, three bases per residue. A codon split by an intron maps to both exons. The count of split codons equals the count recomputed independently from the exon model (50 at design). The strand is read from the annotation, never assumed | A residue has other than three bases; a base is used twice; the split-codon counts disagree; or the strand is hard-coded |

versions.text:
| G4 | **Independent descriptions agree.** Sample variants, by a rule fixed now:
• ClinVar VCV000012964;
• the RYR1 variants ClinVar lists as reviewed by an expert panel, taken at even spacing along GRCh38 to give 20;
• the first intronic variant and the first split-codon variant in position order, if the set has none.
For each, ClinVar's GRCh38 position, its `c.` description and its `p.` description all agree with the map. An intronic variant maps to no residue | Any disagreement |

versions.text: | G5 | **Coordinates carry their assembly.** A genome position given without its assembly, or on GRCh37, is refused. A GRCh37 position appears only as a cross-reference quoted from its source | Any position is used without its assembly |

versions.text: | G6 | **The archive's recorded exon map.** *Added 2026-09-28, after G1–G5 were committed (`79ff30b`), on re-reading the archive at the operator's prompting. It adds a comparison and loosens nothing.* The archive holds a coordinate-derived exon→residue map for all 106 exons on the same transcript and protein (`what/references/ryr1_exon_domain_map.md`, with its data bundle; read-only). Our re-derived map gives the same residue range for each exon, and reproduces the five published HGVS→exon anchors the archive records: R614C→17, R530H→15, Ser2843→54, I4898T→102, A2437V→45. The archive is a quarry, not a source (SO-DOMAIN-10): our map is built from our own logged calls first, and only then compared | Any exon's residue range differs, or any anchor lands in a different exon. The difference is investigated; either side may be wrong. A difference traced to a different transcript or assembly on the archive's side is recorded and dismissed, not tuned away |

versions.text: | A1 | **One human numbering.** UniProt P21817-1 (sequence version 3) and RefSeq NP_000531.2 (MANE Select) are identical, residue for residue. versions.text: | A3 | **Two aligners agree.** Global alignments from two independent implementations (method A: Biopython's `PairwiseAligner`; method B: a separately written program chosen in objective 4, not a wrapper around A) give the same residue pairs | Any pair differs, unless the difference is a gap that can be placed in more than one position with an equal score. Each such residue is listed and flagged *ambiguous* in the mapping |

Aligned pairs + human-only residues = 5,038, and aligned pairs + rabbit-only residues = 5,037 | A residue in an indel maps to a residue, or either sum fails |

Where the source states non-conservation, a differing residue is expected, not a failure | A stated correspondence is not reproduced by the mapping. versions.text:
# O4: what the mouse mapping's checks read. Proposed by a trial on 2026-10-06 (a fork of
# [a working record, not public]); nothing here is pre-registered until the main session commits it, and
# `channelscope m01 check-mapping` cannot read it as it stands (see `runner`).
# - A3, A4, A5: M01's criteria as written, with planted faults fitted to this alignment (M01's own faults name
#   human-rabbit positions).
# - A9: M01's criterion, with CQ-02's answers filtered to this mapping: CQ-02 answers once per mapping, so once mouse
#   and pig sit beside rabbit, a human residue has three answers.
# - A8: validation, the table's checksum against its record, and a re-run from the graph before the build. M01's
#   re-run from a named commit and its UniProt replay (a network call) wait for the real build.
# - A6, A7, A11 do not apply as written (rabbit's papers; [a peer]'s human-rabbit figure; the archive's rabbit table).
#   Stand-ins below, each a statement already held in this vault, never fetched for this.
build_inputs: curation/build_o4_mapping_mouse.yaml
runner: "channelscope o4 check-mapping (how/runtime/channelscope/src/channelscope/o4.py), written on 2026-10-06 after this file was, since M01's run_mapping_checks reads A6's rabbit list, A7's figure and A11's rabbit table, and its faults name human-rabbit positions"
a9_human_positions: [1, 5038, 614, 4938]
controls:
  - id: O4-mouse-gate
    human: "4938"
    object: "4935"
    residue: I
    source: "O2's reading by flanking sequence in each UniProt entry ([a working note, not public], Part 2): human I4938, mouse I4935"
a6_stand_in:
  - id: O4-mouse-01
    human: "4898"
    object: "4895"
    residue: I
    snapshot: what/references/_snapshots/zvaritch_ryr1_it_heterozygote_2009.html
    quotation: "Ryr1 I4895T/wt (IT/+) mice express a knockin mutation corresponding to the human I4898T EC-uncoupling mutation"
a7_stand_in: "none held in this vault; proposed: identity and pair count from a third, independently written aligner, or an independent check like [a peer]'s of 2026-10-04"
a11: "not applicable: the archive's grounding note gives human-to-rabbit and human-to-pig tables only"
